conviction_note: The Q3 guide was sized on $3.75/gal fuel with Aug-Sep spot assumed at $3.85, while Gulf Coast jet spot printed $4.08-4.70 in September. That points to Q3 EPS at or below the bottom of the $0.00-1.00 guide and a Q4 guide set at Delta's $4.25+ all-in fuel. Against that, Delta's 15% Q3 unit revenue and ~20% Q4 revenue growth suggest fares are passing fuel through, and the stock is already -17% in 20 days and 2% off its 52-week low with ~11% of float short. The findings net to -0.6 and the scaled number is -0.48 (p_up 47 on an 8% absolute move). The near-zero lean is the honest read: the fuel overshoot is public and partly priced, and the reaction history (5 of 7 prints down) argues against a relief rally.

Street EPS consensus is disputed: the sweep says ~$0.35-0.59, and MarketBeat quoted $1.22 at the time of the guide. Stockanalysis (updated 2026-10-19, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/alk/forecast/) shows FY26 EPS of -3.47 on 13 analysts; after H1 at -2.60 that implies H2 of about -0.87, i.e. the street may already model a Q4 loss. No sourced Q3 revenue consensus. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue/RASM against the company's 'low double digits' RASM guide. The EPS bar is unsourced beyond the company range, so the guidance-dependent findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest about 12.1M shares, ~10-11% of float, 3.7 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (11.5M, 5.1 days at 09-15) per curvedtrading (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/alk/short-interest/). Benzinga showed a 10.9% short float around 09-09. That is elevated, not crowded (below the 18-23% squeeze cases). Baseline skew -0.09 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.94, event-implied move 8.9%, run-up -8.2% over 5d and -17.2% over 20d, -42% from the 52-week high, +2.2% from the 52-week low.

findings.finding: Q3 fuel ran well above the guide's assumption. The guide assumed $3.60/gal for July and $3.85 spot for Aug-Sep. Gulf Coast jet spot was $4.08 on 2026-09-04, peaked at $4.705 on 09-15 and was $4.40 on 09-29, after $3.43-3.92 in August, and West Coast jet traded at a premium to NYMEX after the California refinery closures. A quarter-average overrun of ~$0.15-0.30/gal on ~380-400m gallons is ~$60-120m pre-tax, or ~$0.35-0.70 of EPS at the guide's 35% tax and 113.5m shares. That puts Q3 adjusted EPS near or below the $0.00 bottom of the guide, against a sweep consensus of ~$0.35-0.59.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: Q2 adjusted -0.92 beat a ~-1.00 bar, and the stock fell 2.4% on the weak Q3 guide. April 2026: Q1 -1.68 beat the guide midpoint, stock -4.8%. Beats on the reported quarter have not been bought; the guide drives the move.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The spot rise is public and the stock is -17% in 20 days, but the company has not updated its Q3 guide since July (the 2026-09-29 investor-day 8-K carried no near-term guide), and Benzinga/sweep estimates in the $0.35-0.59 range sit above what the fuel arithmetic gives. If fully priced, the consensus would sit near zero or negative.
findings.independence: FRED weekly Gulf Coast jet (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/WJFUELUSGULF): 3.431 (08-07) to 4.082 (09-04). GlobalAir via search: $4.705 on 09-15. Delta absorbed >$500m of fuel above its July guide in Q3 (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx?type=ern). The West Coast premium (S&P Global, https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/crude-oil/052026-californias-refinery-closures-create-volatile-fuel-prices-supply-gaps) is a proxy and makes ALK's overrun likely larger than the Gulf series shows.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide will be set at much higher fuel than the Q3 guide's $3.75. Delta guided Q4 all-in fuel at ~$4.25/gal on 2026-10-09 and cut FY26 EPS to $5.10-5.60 from $6.50-7.50. Brent was trading near $100 in mid-October (Kalshi weekly contracts put 63% on >$99.99 for 10-16). ALK's own investor-day deck (2026-09-29) says free cash flow is positive only below $3.25/gal and shows 2027 EPS of $5-6 at $3.25. At >$4.25 West Coast fuel, a Q4 loss guide is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul 2026: a Q3 guide of $0-1 against $1.22 consensus took the stock -2.4%. Apr 2026: suspended FY guidance plus a Q2 loss guide, -4.8%. Oct 2025: -6.1%. Weak guides have sold off moderately, not violently.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Stockanalysis FY26 consensus of -3.47 implies H2 ≈ -0.87, consistent with a modelled Q4 loss, and the stock is at its 52-week low. What remains is whether ALK's West Coast fuel premium and 4.5x 2026 leverage (investor day) make the Q4 guide worse than the street's Q4 number, which I cannot source.
findings.independence: ALK investor-day deck, 8-K 2026-09-29 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/766421/000076642126000043/a2026investordaypresenta.htm): 'Fuel remains the largest near-term headwind', FCF positive only below $3.25/gal. Kalshi Brent weekly (https://kalshi.com/markets/kxbrentw/brent-oil/kxbrentw-26oct1617), snapshot undated. Shares the fuel fact with finding 1 but lands on a different line (Q4 guide, not Q3 actual).

findings.finding: Peers say fares are passing fuel through. Delta's Q3 2026 unit revenue rose 15% year over year and it guided Q4 total revenue up ~20%, with 'demand remains strong'. United said in July it would recover 80-90% of the fuel increase in Q3 and 100% by Q4, with Q3/Q4 TRASM above Q2's +12.1%. ALK guided Q3 RASM up 'low double digits' with Hawaii a 2-3 point drag, so a RASM print at or above the top of that range and a firm Q4 RASM guide are plausible offsets to fuel.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan 2026: the one clearly positive revenue/outlook print took the stock +4.1%. Jan 2025: +2.2%. Revenue strength has been bought modestly when the guide held.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock's -17% 20-day slide prices fuel cost, not fare recovery. If fare pass-through were priced, ALK would not sit 2% off its 52-week low while Delta guided Q4 revenue +20%. ALK, however, is more leisure/Hawaii-exposed than Delta (Q2 revenue missed estimates), so the transmission is a peer proxy.
findings.independence: United's 8-K ex99.2 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000135/ual_erx06302026xex992.htm), July 2026: Q4 TRASM growth above Q2's 12.1%, 100% fuel recovery by Q4. Company-independent from Delta. United reports the same evening (10-20 amc), so its print is a simultaneous, correlated read inside the window.

findings.finding: The 2026-09-29 investor day reset the medium-term frame lower. Adjusted net debt/EBITDAR is 4.5x in 2026 and ~4.7x in 2027 (from 2.4x in 2024), buybacks are cut to ~$250m in 2026 and ~$180m in 2027 (from $570m in 2025), 'restoring balance sheet strength is our top priority', and >$10 EPS is now tied to a $2.50/gal fuel assumption. Management is likely to repeat this on the call, capping any multiple re-rating from the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print carried a leverage or buyback change; the investor day itself coincided with the 20-day slide (-17%), which suggests it was already absorbed.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is a public 8-K three weeks old and the stock has fallen since. The residual is the risk that the call quantifies 2027 at current fuel (stockanalysis FY27 consensus $3.38, already below the deck's $5-6 at $3.25 fuel).
findings.independence: Stockanalysis FY27 EPS consensus 3.38 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/alk/forecast/) is consistent with the street already being below management's frame. Same company document as part of finding 2's independence; the lines differ (capital return vs Q4 guide).

findings.finding: Positioning is washed out into the print: -17.2% over 20 days and -8.2% over 5 days, 2.2% above the 52-week low and 42% below the high, short interest ~12.1M shares (~10-11% of float, 3.7 days to cover at 09-30, up from 10.7M in August), skew balanced at -0.09. A Q4 guide that is merely 'less bad than Delta implies' has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 5 of the last 7 prints fell (median |move| 4.8%), including after reported-quarter beats in Apr and Jul 2026. The name has not historically rewarded washed-out setups, which keeps this small.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the market's own state, not information. What would look different if a bounce were expected: call skew bid (skew is -0.09, flat) and a stabilising tape (it fell 8% in the last 5 sessions).
findings.independence: The sealed baseline's own tape (run-up and 52-week distance, as of 2026-10-20). Equibles 10.7M short / 9.6% float on 2026-08-19 (https://equibles.com/stocks/alk/shortinterest) shows the short base rising.

findings.finding: Network mix is moving toward the Hawaii recovery the company described in July ('loads are recovering and new bookings are coming in at system level yields'; Hawaii a 2-3 point Q3 RASM headwind). Cirium schedules show Q4 2026 Hawaii seats from the mainland +6% year over year and Mexico seats -30%. That supports a narrowing Hawaii drag in the Q4 RASM guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hawaii weakness was cited in the Q1 and Q2 2026 releases, both of which sold off (-4.8%, -2.4%); there is no history of Hawaii improvement being rewarded yet.

baseline_tension: The fuel findings agree with the run-up (-17% in 20 days, at the 52-week low) and are therefore mostly priced. Balanced skew (-0.09) gives no directional lean to contradict. The positive offsets (fare pass-through, washed-out positioning) cut against the run-up but run into a reaction history that sells prints. Net, p_up sits just under 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced): the Q4 street bar cannot be sourced to two agreeing estimates (FY26 -3.47 on one site, sweep 0.35-0.59 for Q3), so both Q4-guide findings were capped smaller: the fuel Q4 guide -1.0 to -0.8 and the peer fare pass-through +1.0 to +0.8.
Rule 5 (proxy smaller): the Delta/United fare pass-through is a peer proxy, which is part of why it moved from +1.0 to +0.8 (applied once, together with rule 6).
Rules 1 and 7 (reaction function; positioning): 5 of 7 prints fell, including after reported-quarter beats, so the washed-out positioning finding went from +1.0 to +0.6 and p_up from 48 to 47.
Rule 7: short interest checked (~11% of float, 3.7 days) before the negatives; elevated but not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk further.

The Q3 fuel overshoot (-1.0) and the investor-day finding (-0.4) were left unchanged: the first rests on the company's own stated fuel assumption against a public price series, and the second is already small for being public.
